questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why doctors now prescribe time in forests
How wood is being used in new ways to build a greener future
The history of shipbuilding in Britain
Why forests in Britain are disappearing faster than ever
questions.why: Neil says they'll hear how wood is being used in new ways to build a greener future.

options: Being calm among trees and using all your senses
Swimming in lakes inside forests
Cutting down old trees so that new ones can be planted
Taking a bath with plant oils
questions.why: Beth says it means being calm and quiet amongst trees, observing nature with all your senses.

questions.q: How much of Britain was forest in Roman times?
options: Almost all of it
About 10%
As much as 40%
About 85%
questions.why: Beth says as much as 40% of the land was forest.

questions.q: What has mostly replaced timber in modern buildings?
options: Bamboo, hemp and other plants
Plastic and glass
Stone and clay
Brick, concrete and steel
questions.why: Beth says in modern times man-made materials like brick, concrete and steel are mostly used.

questions.q: What evidence does architect Michael Ramage give about wooden buildings?
options: Children in wooden schools focus better and feel calmer
Wooden hospitals are cheaper to build
Wooden houses last much longer than houses made of brick
People in wooden offices work longer hours
questions.why: He says children in wooden schools have greater concentration and lower stress.

questions.q: What other reason for building with wood does Beth give?
options: It is easier to transport
It is much cheaper than steel and quicker to build with
It looks more traditional
It stores carbon, which helps fight climate change
questions.why: She says the carbon which wood captures helps combat climate change.

questions.q: What does Michael Ramage suggest about materials like bamboo and hemp?
options: They are only really good for making things like rope and cloth
They are too weak for large buildings
They could replace steel and concrete if used well
They should only be used for houses
questions.why: He talks about using them intelligently as replacements for steel and concrete.

questions.q: Where is the world's tallest wooden skyscraper?
options: In a city in Norway
In Milwaukee, USA
In Japan
In London
questions.why: Neil says the tallest, at 87 metres, is in Milwaukee, USA.
